6 photosTechnical & Legal

Electrical faults are invisible until they fail — or cause fires. Using SIRIM-calibrated testers, we measure earthing, insulation and polarity, inspect the distribution board, and flag safety issues before they become dangerous.

What's included

  • Earth resistance testing
  • Insulation resistance testing
  • Polarity & wiring check
  • Distribution board (DB) inspection
  • Socket & switch functionality test

What you receive

  • Electrical test report with readings
  • Safety issue list by severity
  • Rectification recommendations

Why It Matters

Electrical Faults Stay Invisible Until They Don't

Fire & Shock Risk Found Early

Loose terminations and failed insulation are silent until they cause a fire

Measured Values, Not Guesses

Earth, insulation and load values recorded — an electrician's "looks fine" is not a test

Readings in Your Report

Every test result documented with its value — comparable at any future inspection

Leverage With the Developer

A failed earth or insulation reading is not something a developer can argue away

Independent of the Wiring Contractor

We test the work; we do not sell the rewiring — no reason to inflate findings

Especially for Older Homes

Ageing installations and past DIY alterations are where most failures are found

How It Works

4 Stages of an Electrical Inspection

Measured values, not opinions — every test recorded with its actual reading

1

Distribution Board Review

DB condition, circuit labelling, protective devices and signs of overheating

2

Instrument Testing

Earth resistance, insulation resistance and polarity measured and recorded

3

Load & Functionality

Clamp meter load readings, RCCB trip test and point-by-point functionality checks

4

Report With Readings

Every value recorded, findings classified, rectification recommendations included

Result Classification

Every Test Result Classified

You will know exactly which findings are safe, which need work, and which cannot wait

Pass

Reading within acceptable range — no action required

Marginal

Acceptable but close to limit — monitor and re-test later

Fail

Outside acceptable range — rectification by a licensed electrician required

Immediate Danger

Shock or fire risk present — isolate and rectify without delay
